name: Puluwat
confidence_why: Elbert (1974), the only first-hand grammar of Puluwat, describes stress as "about even on all syllables" with only scattered exceptions (final vowel in CVCV words, h-initial syllables) and gives no placement rule, so the record stays undetermined; Elbert's 1972 dictionary and Jackson's 1983 Trukic dissertation say nothing about Puluwat word stress, and StressTyp2's quantity-sensitive coding is a reinterpretation of that same Elbert 1974 passage.
catalog_citation: Elbert, Samuel H. 1974. Puluwat Grammar. Pacific Linguistics, Series B, No. 29. Canberra: Australian National University.
catalog_locator: pp.13-14, ch. 'Phonology', section 'Notes on Stress' (PDF pages 19-20 of)
catalog_quote: Notes on Stress. Stress is about even on all syllables, with these noticeable exceptions (vowels strongly stressed are capitalised; excrescent vowels with weak stress are shown with a brev): (1) CVCV words seem stressed on the final vowels: hanA hibiscus flower, ... yifA? where?, ... yiwE then. (2) Syllables beginning with h- are usually stressed: yapwahAaló to dry out, pahAló to drift away, yekúhÚ rak just a little. (3) The excrescent vowel is weak and unstressed (except after h-). ... (e) A number of words of the shape C1V1C2V2C3V3 have stress on V1 and V3 and weak stress on V2: ...

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim at the stated place on held page scan of Elbert 1974 pp.13-14. (2) The deciding source is the language's only reference grammar (Pacific Linguistics B-29, 1974, fieldwork-based, dedicated stress section); the only other Glottolog description (Lynch 2002 sketch) is derived from it and restates the same stress note; StressTyp2's conflicting quantity-sensitive coding cites the same Elbert 1974, so the contradiction is interpretive, and our not determinable (hedged 'about even on all syllables' with non-culminative h-onset and CVCV-final exceptions, no weight statement) is the more literal reading. (3) Elbert 1972 dictionary downloaded from the open PL archive: silent on stress. No Puluwatese-specific phonology/instrumental study surfaced in Glottolog or the UH ScholarSpace repository; Wishlis

sources.citation: Elbert, Samuel H. 1972. Puluwat Dictionary. Pacific Linguistics, Series C, No. 24. Canberra: Australian National University. (410 pp.)
sources.quote: None. The only prosody-adjacent line is orthographic: 'The five letters with accent marks (á, é, ó, ú, í) follow the same letters without accent marks' (Introduction p.v) -- these diacritics mark vowel quality, not stress. The Preface defers grammar to 'the grammar, still in preparation' (= Elbert 1974).
sources.locator: Front matter: Preface p.iv, Introduction pp.v-x
